10.words:
First thing on June 1st, Nora Murphy walks up to you in the street.
Nora Murphy stands at the edge of the room, holding a folded flyer from your campaign. // Nora Murphy: I know I'm not one of the big names. I won't take long.
Put me down to speak at the next public meeting. I want you to know why. [Replies: I'll read what you send. Put your name on it so I can write back. | My scheduler will find you a slot. Give her your number. | I'll hear you out. I can't promise a vote because of a donation, any size. | Not today. Catch me after the session.] // Nora Murphy: MIRA PARSONS
I'll read what you send. Put your name on it so I can write back.
Thank you. I didn't expect anyone to pick up.

01.words: Friends, I'm glad to be here today. Honestly, I think the best part of this country is still ahead of us. This country's never been finished. Every generation gets handed the job, and now it's ours. // I'm from Wyoming, and I've seen what neighbors can do when they've got a reason to hope. I accept this trust gladly, and I want you to hold me to the best of what I've said.

06.words:
First thing on June 6th, Julia Lambert catches you at school.
It's the last day of the school year. Julia Lambert has been meaning to say something. // Julia Lambert: Last day. Can you believe it?
Do you know what you're doing next? [Replies: Something worth doing. I'll know it when I find it. | What are you doing? You go first. | When I know, you'll know. | Ask me again in a month.] // Julia Lambert: MIRA PARSONS
Something worth doing. I'll know it when I find it.
That sounds like you. What made you decide? [Replies: Something worth doing. I'll know it when I see it. | I'll let you know once I figure it out. | Check back in a month. | I have to run. I wish you the best.] // Julia Lambert: MIRA PARSONS
Something worth doing. I'll know it when I see it.
Here? Really? What would you even do? [Replies: Something that matters. I'll know it when I see it. | I'll tell you when I figure it out. | Ask me in a month. | I have to go. Good luck, really.] // Julia Lambert: MIRA PARSONS
Something that matters. I'll know it when I see it.
Good. You'll be good at it.

07.words:
First thing on January 23rd, you head out, and Riley Riley comes over.
The governor's speech is over, and Riley Riley has had the last word on it. Now they want yours. // Riley Riley: Hello, Mira. You were in the room. Did you hear what I said back?
The governor asked for a lot today. Are you with the governor, or with us? [Replies: I heard the same speech you did. I'll judge each ask when it comes up as a bill. | What would you do instead? That's the part I didn't hear. | I'll hear you out before the vote. That's a promise. | No. Not on the day of the speech.] // Riley Riley: MIRA PARSONS
I heard the same speech you did. I'll judge each ask when it comes up as a bill.
I'll keep making the case, with you or without you. [Replies: The governor has a point on a few things. I'm not ready to say which. | I'm not picking a side in a hallway. | Let's pick this up another time, when it's quieter.] // Riley Riley: MIRA PARSONS
The governor has a point on a few things. I'm not ready to say which.
The governor's asks will come back to us as bills, and we'll have to vote on every one. [Replies: Some of it I liked and some of it I didn't. I'm not going to pretend it was all one thing. | I'll vote the way my district needs, not the way either of you asks. | I have to get to my next meeting.] // Riley Riley: MIRA PARSONS
Some of it I liked and some of it I didn't. I'm not going to pretend it was all one thing.
Think about who sent you here. They heard that speech too.
That was all I wanted to say. Take care.

08.words:
Sofia Pierce: First thing on May 29th, you head to the City Clerk's office to ask about running. Sofia Pierce comes over to the counter. // Sofia Pierce: What can I do for you? [Replies: I want to run for Council member. November 4, 2025 · Held by Stephanie Gordon | I want to run for Mayor. November 4, 2025 · Held by Emma Sellers] // Sofia Pierce: MIRA PARSONS
I want to run for Council member.
So you're running for Council member. You'd serve 4 years. There's no primary for this one, so it all comes down to November 4. You'd have a seat on the Almont Village Council, voting on the budget and every ordinance that comes before it. You've got until July 22 to get it all back to me. [Replies: Alright. I'll take the papers and get started.] // MIRA PARSONS
Alright. I'll take the papers and get started.
YOU ARE ON THE BALLOT
